source: Seoul National University Korean 2B, Unit 10, tracks 02-11

lines.ko: 한국 음식 중에서 뭘 제일 좋아해요?

tracks.secEn: Steven and Jeongwoo pick a restaurant

lines.ko: 이 근처에 있는 식당 중에서 어디가 제일 좋아?
다음 주 토요일이 우리 반 친구 생일이라서 친구들하고 같이 저녁 먹으려고.
다 잘 먹는데 친구들 중에 매운 음식을 잘 못 먹는 사람이 있어.
그럼 사거리에 있는 서울식당이 어때? 서울식당은 갈비가 유명한데 다른 음식도 다 맛있고 값도 비싸지 않아.
주말에는 항상 사람이 많으니까 예약해야 될 거야.
아니요, 닭고기는 좋아하는데 삼계탕은 별로 안 좋아해요.
이 식당은 삼계탕이 맛있는데 한번 먹어 볼래?
음, 난 닭고기는 좋아하는데 삼계탕은 별로 안 좋아해.
그래? 그럼 감자탕 어때? 안 먹어 봤으면 한번 먹어 봐.

tracks.noteEn: The unit page prints the three comprehension statements, not the conversation itself. The 듣기 지문 at the back of the book carries the transcript; until it is in, this is listen-only.
Same as track 08: the page asks what was ordered and what it cost but does not print the words. Waiting on the 듣기 지문 page.

keep: a whole sentence someone would actually say
5-24 syllables, the same band Unit 14 settled on
carries something you can only write correctly if you know something — this chapter's grammar (N 중에(서), 반말, V-(으)ㄹ래요, A-(으)ㄴ데/V-는데), a gap between sound and spelling, or a unit headword
drop: fixed courtesies and bare acknowledgements — 아니요, 그래?, 좋아, 응, 음
anything under 5 syllables: 식당은 왜, 뭐 먹을래, 맛이 어때, 입에 맞아 all fall here, and the last two are a loss worth naming — 입에 맞다 is a unit headword, but four syllables leaves nothing to decide
a printed line with a numeral read aloud — 감자탕 2인분 주세요. The syllable count cannot be derived from the text, so the pace check that verifies the cut has nothing to measure

three turns of 28-43 syllables whose internal pauses fall mid-clause: 다음 주 토요일이…, 서울식당은 갈비가 유명한데…, and 음, 난 닭고기는… — the last of which also repeats track 06 almost word for word in a different register
the two tracks with no printed script, 08 and 09
filter.splitAtClause: Nine printed turns open with something the row does not want — 아니요, 그래?, 좋아, 응, 음 — or run two sentences together, and in every case the narrator pauses at that boundary, so the split lands on the recording’s own break rather than on the punctuation. Each child names its parent in splitFrom.

dictation.note: This unit's 발음 page is question intonation, which a dictation cannot test — nothing about a rising or falling pitch changes what you write. The set therefore leans on the chapter's four grammar patterns and on the liaison and assimilation that happen anyway.

items.ko: 한국 음식 중에서 뭘 제일 좋아해요?
items.en: Which Korean food do you like best?
items.why: The pattern the page teaches. 좋아해요 is said [조아해요] — the ㅎ drops out between vowels and leaves nothing to write from, so the 좋 has to come from knowing 좋다.

items.en: I like bulgogi best.
items.why: The shortest answer the pattern takes. 불고기를 runs together as [불고기를] with the ㄹ carrying across, and 좋아해요 is [조아해요] again — the same disappearing ㅎ, in the sentence right after it.

items.en: What are you doing after class?
items.why: 끝나고 is said [끈나고]: the ㅌ of 끝 closes to [ㄷ] and then becomes ㄴ before the ㄴ of 나. Two letters written, one heard, and neither of them the one on the page.

items.en: I am going to Myeongdong to meet a friend.
items.why: 갈 거야 is said [갈 꺼야] — the ㄱ tenses after the ㄹ of a -(으)ㄹ ending, which is a rule about the ending rather than about the word. Write 갈 커야 or 갈 거야 and only one of them is right.

items.ko: 이 근처에 있는 식당 중에서 어디가 제일 좋아?
items.en: Of the restaurants near here, which is the best?
items.why: The unit grammar in 반말. 있는 is said [인는] — the ㅆ closes to [ㄷ] and then assimilates to ㄴ — and 식당 is [식땅], the ㄷ tensing after the ㄱ.

items.en: What kind of food do they like?
items.why: The chapter’s other pattern, used as a question rather than a contrast. 음식을 is [음시글] and 좋아하는데 is [조아하는데], so the two words carrying the meaning are both spelled for the root and not for the sound.

items.ko: 다 잘 먹는데 친구들 중에 매운 음식을 잘 못 먹는 사람이 있어.
items.en: They all eat well, but one of them cannot manage spicy food.
items.why: Both unit patterns in one sentence. 먹는데 is said [멍는데] and 먹는 is [멍는] — the ㄱ becomes ㅇ before the ㄴ, twice, and 못 먹는 comes out [몬 멍는].

items.en: How about the Seoul Restaurant at the crossroads?
items.why: 사거리에 and 식당이 both hand their final consonant to the next syllable — [사거리에], [식땅이] — and 식당 tenses as it did two rows ago. A row about hearing where one word stops.
items.splitFrom: 그럼 사거리에 있는 서울식당이 어때? 서울식당은 갈비가 유명한데 다른 음식도 다 맛있고 값도 비싸지 않아.

items.en: Should we book ahead?
items.why: 예약을 is said [예야글] and 할까 keeps its tense ㄲ from the -(으)ㄹ까 ending itself. 미리 is a unit headword and the sentence is the one place the chapter uses it.

items.ko: 주말에는 항상 사람이 많으니까 예약해야 될 거야.
items.en: Weekends are always busy, so we will have to book.
items.why: 많으니까 is said [마느니까]: the ㅎ of the ㄶ cluster vanishes and only the ㄴ carries over. 될 거야 tenses the same way 갈 거야 did on track 03.

items.en: I will have kalguksu.
items.why: The pattern at its shortest, in 반말. 먹을래 is said [머글래] — the ㄱ hops into the next syllable — so the 먹 you write is not where you hear it.

items.en: Do you like samgyetang?
items.why: 삼계탕 is a unit headword and 좋아해요 is [조아해요] once more. Short enough to write in one go, which is what makes the vanished ㅎ the only thing to get wrong.

items.ko: 닭고기는 좋아하는데 삼계탕은 별로 안 좋아해요.
items.en: I like chicken, but I am not keen on samgyetang.
items.why: 닭고기는 is said [닥꼬기는]: the ㄺ cluster gives up its ㄹ, the ㄱ that is left tenses the ㄱ after it. Three changes before the contrast even starts.
items.splitFrom: 아니요, 닭고기는 좋아하는데 삼계탕은 별로 안 좋아해요.

items.en: Steven, what will you have?
items.why: The pattern as it is actually used — across a table, in 반말, with a name in front of it. 먹을래 is [머글래].

items.en: There is a lot to choose from.
items.why: 많네 is said [만네]: the ㅎ of the ㄶ cluster disappears and the ㄴ that remains turns the following ㄴ into a double one. Five syllables, and the middle two are the whole exercise.

items.en: What is good here?
items.why: 맛있어 is said [마시써] — the ㅅ of 맛 carries into 있 and the ㅆ that follows sounds identical, so the spelling has to come from knowing both words rather than from the sound.

items.ko: 이 식당은 삼계탕이 맛있는데 한번 먹어 볼래?
items.en: The samgyetang here is good — will you try it?
items.why: Both of the chapter’s second-half patterns in one turn. 맛있는데 is [마신는데]: the ㅅ moves across, then the ㅆ closes and assimilates to ㄴ.

items.en: How about gamjatang then?
items.why: 감자탕 is a unit headword, and 어때 is the 반말 of 어때요 — the form the whole 말하기 page is built on. Nothing changes sound here, which is the point: it is the row that checks you are listening to words and not only to rules.
items.splitFrom: 그래? 그럼 감자탕 어때? 안 먹어 봤으면 한번 먹어 봐.

items.ko: 안 먹어 봤으면 한번 먹어 봐.
items.en: If you have not tried it, give it a go.
items.why: 봤으면 is said [봐쓰면] — the ㅆ carries into the vowel — and 먹어 is [머거], twice in one line. The -아/어 보다 of trying something, which the chapter uses on nearly every page.
items.splitFrom: 그래? 그럼 감자탕 어때? 안 먹어 봤으면 한번 먹어 봐.

items.en: Let us order the gamjatang then.
items.why: 시키자 is 시키다 — a unit headword — in the -자 of 반말 suggestion. The whole ordering scene turns on this verb rather than on 주문하다, which is the polite one.

items.en: A bit hot, but good.
items.why: The chapter’s contrast pattern in five words. 매운데 is the ㅂ-irregular 맵다 with its ㅂ already gone to 우, so the dictionary form is not recoverable from what you hear.

items.en: Is the food to your taste?
items.why: Three liaisons in seven syllables: 음식이 [음시기], 입에 [이베], 맞아 [마자]. 입에 맞다 is a unit headword and this is the sentence the book teaches it in.

items.en: Have you been to that restaurant?
items.why: 식당에 is said [식땅에] — the ㄷ tenses after the ㄱ — and 봤어요 is [봐써요]. The rising intonation is what this page is about, but the spelling is what a dictation catches.

items.en: Where are you going in the holidays?
items.why: 방학에 is [방하게] and 갈 거야 is [갈 꺼야]. Both changes are invisible on the page, and the second one is the same -(으)ㄹ tensing that turned up on tracks 03 and 04.

items.en: What sport do you like?
items.why: 운동을 is said [운동을] with the ㅇ holding, and 좋아해요 is [조아해요] — the chapter’s most frequent disappearing ㅎ, here in a question with an interrogative, which the 발음 page says falls rather than rises.

items.en: What shall we do today?
items.why: 할까 carries its tense ㄲ in the ending itself rather than from a neighbouring consonant — -(으)ㄹ까 is written with ㄲ and said with it. The contrast with 갈 거야, where the tensing is not written, is the reason both are in this set.

items.en: Shall we go and see a film?
items.why: The reply to the row above, and the shortest -(으)ㄹ까 in the chapter. 보러 is the -(으)러 of purpose, which needs a verb of movement after it — and 가다 is exactly that.

listenOnly: Tracks 08 and 09 have no printed script. The pane says so rather than going blank, and no dictation sentence is drawn from them.
